metadata.source_prompt: A quadcopter drone with a camera for aerial photos of my garden

design.summary: Quadcopter, 5 in props on 2207 motors: 0.47 kg take-off, thrust-to-weight 6.6, hover at 15 % throttle, about 10 min

uses: FPV camera, tilted up 25 deg for forward flight
battery strap through the frame slots
rail splices, the star ground and bus hubs

checks.name: flight:prop_clearance

performance.prop: 5 x 4.3 x 3 tri-blade propeller, M5 hub (HQProp 5043 V1S), one
performance.motor: 2207 brushless motor 1750 KV for 5 in props, 4S (e.g. iFlight XING2 2207)
performance.cost_breakdown: parts 248.30 USD, filament 2.41 USD (0.10 kg), fasteners ~4.80 USD, wiring 15.02 USD

assumptions: Thrust and current come from a typical 2207 1750 KV static thrust table with 5 x 4.3 x 3 props on a full 4S pack (estimated; real motors vary by about 10 %). Thrust falls as the pack sags and in forward flight.
The frame is printed flat in PETG (or better, CF-nylon). It is stiff enough for gentle flying; it does not survive crashes like a carbon frame. Balance the props.

The flight controller runs Betaflight, INAV or ArduPilot: it does the stabilisation. Configure motor order, direction (props in), failsafe and the 60 A current limit before the first flight, without props.
Fly where it is legal: in most countries a drone over 250 g must be registered and flown within sight, away from people.
